subject: Post-call: Affordability sprint & token TCO alignment
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@finvera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-04-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Affordability sprint & token TCO alignment

Sarah —

Thanks again for the 45-minute intro this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and the path I propose:

Pain points & goals
- Token spend is the largest cost bucket for your assistant product; current average spend ≈ $35k/month and trending up.
- High call volume with many short, repetitive prompts (support snippets + templated replies).
- SLOs: 95th percentile latency target ≤ 300ms; must not regress user experience.
- Procurement runway: target budget ceiling ~$20k/month for a pilot (constrained this quarter).
- Security/residency: primary data must remain in US regions; SOC2 compliance required.

Suggested levers (high-level TCO impact)
- Intelligent batching for low-latency bursts — estimated 15–35% token/throughput savings depending on concurrency.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeat prompts — estimated 10–25% immediate token reduction on FAQ/support flows.
- Quantized model variant (int8) for non-critical paths — 20–40% per-token cost cut at small quality tradeoffs.
- Routing to a smaller model for short responses and Redwood fallback policies for degraded capacity.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Redwood to deliver a baseline estimate and a short, one-page pilot scope (attached: redwood_baseline-estimate.xlsx, pilot-scope.pdf) — ETA Tuesday 4/18.
2) Run an affordability sprint: 6-week pilot measuring cost delta, latency SLO, and quality on a 5k-user sample.
3) Define success criteria: ≤10% quality degradation (evaluated on your prompt set), ≥25% reduction in per-conversation unit cost, and latency 95p ≤300ms.
4) Procurement/legal touchpoint — you mentioned involving procurement@finvera.com after we share the estimate.

If that aligns, I’ll have Marissa draft the pilot MOU and Tessa scope the integration checklist. Any adjustments to the timeline or success criteria?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_baseline-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet), pilot-scope.pdf (PDF)

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@finvera.com>

Date: 2028-04-15T11:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Affordability sprint & token TCO alignment

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful and mostly aligns with what we heard internally. A few quick clarifications:

- The $35k/month is our current aggregate vendor spend across requests routed through our assistant; procurement has been pushing to get a pilot cost under $20k/month to justify a Q2 commitment.
- For caching: ~40% of requests are repeats or small variations (templates) — if your prefix caching hits that, the savings look promising.
- Latency target is non-negotiable for the user-facing flows; we can accept slightly higher latency for back-office automations.
- Data residency: US-only region is a hard requirement for the pilot. SOC2 report is required before we go to procurement.

Please confirm whether the baseline estimate will show: (a) expected monthly spend during pilot vs status quo, (b) expected per-conversation unit cost after proposed levers, and (c) a short list of integration touchpoints (webhook vs proxy).

If you can provide that by Tuesday we’ll loop procurement and legal and aim to have an internal decision meeting the week of 4/24.

—Sarah
Head of Product, Finvera
